en: "For my new home~ somewhere cooler than here would be nice, mogu~{w}Where should I go, mogu~..."{w}
"Loipes Cave would be good, mogu!!{w}I want you to help me find a big chamber on the very lowest floor of Loipes Cave, mogu!"{w}
note: genshitsu = Wizardry-style chamber/room.

en: "Mogeee!?{w}There's no room for me, moguuu!?{w}Go make room for me, mogu!!"{w}
note: Mogu used as Raizam's first person ('mogu ga hairu basho') rendered as I/me. Presumably the chamber found is too small, so Raizam digs one. | lead: party-full message (no room in the party), as the editorial reviewer read it from context.

en: "I'm all weak from this heat, mogu!{w}I want you to carry delicate little me gently, mogu~"{w}
"Are you ready, mogu?{w}I'm all set, mogu~{w}Let's hurry up and go, mogu~"{w}
Footbath Attendant
note: Glossary form (18 chars, over the ~16 name-box guide); check fit in game.

en: "Heerdahl's famous Footbath Hall is this way!"{w}
note: Editorial: Footbath Hall capitalised as the venue name (as in slice 041, 3033).

en:
"Splash, splash as you walk,
and give your mind and body a re-fre~~~sh!!"{w}
note: Editorial: "heart and body" -> idiomatic "mind and body".

en: "Oh my, you really shouldn't come into a place like this."{w}{p}"What's the matter? Do you want me to play with you?{w}What a hopeless child you are."{w}
note: shouganai ko ne: toying, addresses the party as a child; same tone in 2681. Editorial: fragment order fixed; "incorrigible" too stiff for her toying voice, aligned with 2681 "hopeless child".

en: "In that case, let's have a battle of wits, you and I.{w}If you can win, I'll give you the Breastplate of Intellect."{w}
"Huh?{w}You want me to stop the killing in the arena too?"{w}{p}"How kind of you. Fine, I'll put a stop to it.{w}If you can entertain me some other way... with this battle of wits, that is."{w}
note: The party's request is implied (no choice row); read as the party asking her to end the arena death matches as well.

en: "Let's use this glass of water and some coins."{w}

"The rules are simple.{w}We take turns sinking 1 to 3 coins
into this glass."{w}{p}"Whoever makes the glass overflow first loses.{w}Simple, isn't it?{w}Well then, shall we begin?"{w}
"Ngh...!!{w}That I would...{w}...ever see the day I lose at a game..."{w}{p}"......"{w}
"I accept it. I've lost this game.{w}You were good, all of you.{w}As promised, I'll give you the Breastplate of Intellect."{w}
note: Editorial: stilted tense ("I lose this game") made natural.

en:
[Key Item]
You obtained the Breastplate of Intellect.{w}

note: Editorial: "some other fun thing" -> natural phrasing.

en: "Losing stings, but...{w}I haven't felt like that in a long time.{w}...It was so much fun."{w}{p}"Don't tell me this is goodbye, okay?{w}You'll come and play again, won't you? I'll be waiting..."{w}
note: Editorial: iwanaide yo ne is a soft plea; "Don't you dare" was too forceful (accuracy open item).

en: "There, all over.{w}I thought you'd hold out a little longer.{w}You hopeless child."{w}{p}"Come again.{w}I'll play with you any time."{w}
...Rout Mistress?
note: Prompt object unstated in the source; name used to avoid a gendered pronoun.

en: "...What a boring bunch.{w}I got my hopes up for nothing. Do as you please."{w}
note: Editorial: "What a waste of my hopes" unidiomatic for kitai shite son shita.

en: "Oh my, back again?{w}Fine, I'll take you on as many times as you like."{w}

"You came to see me. I'm so glad.{w}What will it be today?
I've prepared this kind of game too..."{w}
"Won't you try it?{w}I owe you some payback for my loss, after all.{w}Mmhehe."{w}
Mistress Bud
note: Glossary note form. tsubomi = bud, i.e. the Mistress's successor-in-training.

en: "Welcome to Heerdahl.{w}...The previous Mistress?{w}They left, saying the fun had been spoiled."{w}{p}"A game is fun because it has rules.{w}I have been instructed to ask those who cannot share in that fun to leave."{w}{p}"...Good day to you, you boring people."{w}
note: 'They' = the previous Mistress (gender not established). Shown after the party chose to rout Mistress (2684). Editorial: awkward split sentence (and mid-phrase line break) recast; formal register kept.

en: {0A:0003:000F}'s alignment changed to Evil.{w}
note: seikaku = alignment, as in slice 000.

en: {0A:0003:000F}'s alignment changed to Good.{w}
"Now, your turn.{w}How many will you put in for me, I wonder?{w}Hehe... I can't wait~"{w}
note: The coin game is written as sexual double entendre (ireru = put in); English keeps 'put in' throughout so the innuendo carries at the same strength.

en:
"Come on, it's your turn.{w}Put in as many as you like,
if you think you can!"{w}
note: ireru mono nara = 'if you can manage to put them in'; rendered as a taunt. Accuracy: ireru mono nara = 'if you can manage to put them in' (doubt about the party's ability), not 'take it' (receiving).

en: Choose how many coins.
You put in 1 coin.{w}
"Oh my, is that all?{w}...You can put in more, you know?{w}Or would you rather enjoy it slowly?"{w}
"What are you holding back for?{w}You really want to put in more, don't you!"{w}
You put in 2 coins.{w}
"Come on, you have to put it in gently...{w}Could it be you're nervous?{w}Shall I take the lead for you... hehe."{w}
"Would you stop copying me?{w}You nasty thing...!!"{w}
note: iyarashii hito: both 'sly' (mirroring her move) and 'lewd'; 'nasty' covers both.

en: You put in 3 coins.{w}
"No way, you're putting in that many?{w}It's going to overflow, honestly...{w}You're so impatient."{w}

"Hey, stop it!{w}If you put that many in all at once... ah, no...
I can't believe it... no... not like this..."{w}
"My turn. Now then..."{w}
"My turn..."{w}
Mistress put in 1 coin.{w}
Mistress put in 2 coins.{w}
Mistress put in 3 coins.{w}

"Coming to a place like Heerdahl, and even playing
little games like this with me... are you sure that's okay?{w}If we're doing this, let's enjoy it all the way."{w}
note: Accuracy: Heerdahl nanka ni = dismissive 'a place like Heerdahl', not distance.

en: "How about this much?{w}...Still fine?{w}Then I'll torment you some m-o-r-e~"{w}
note: ijimete a-ge-ru: syllable-split teasing kept as m-o-r-e.

en: "What's wrong?{w}You won't win if you let your eyes wander, you know?{w}Not that I mind how much you look at me... hmm?"{w}
"Come at me for real, okay?{w}This is a game for two to enjoy.{w}I want to feel those shivers again, it's been so long..."{w}

"...Hey, once this game is over, you know,
how about we try a different kind of play next?{w}I bet you'll get hooked... mmhehehe."{w}
"Me, beaten by mere adventurers?{w}I won't accept it, I won't accept... this!{w}Ngh... ugh...!"{w}
"Now hold on a minute...???{w}This is going badly...{w}I have to do something... Tch!!"{w}
"You're pretty good...{w}Maybe I should get serious too?"{w}

The moment you put in your coins,
the water overflowed from the glass!!{w}
"Oh my~, did it come spilling out?{w}Look at you, spilling so mu~ch... tee-hee."{w}
note: Editorial: kusukusu = "tee-hee", as Mistress in slice 028 (6055); line made spoken.

en: "Ahh...{w}No, hold it in... noooo...!"{w}
note: Her own losing line: 'dame yo, gaman shite' read as her pleading with herself/the glass; innuendo kept.

en:
The moment Mistress put in the coins,
the water overflowed from the glass!!{w}
note: No possessive pronoun: Mistress's gender is not established. Editorial: "put in coins" read clipped; article added, still no pronoun.

en: Put in 1 coin
Put in 2 coins
Put in 3 coins
Echo
"Milk~!{w}Anybody want some milk!?{w}Echo's milk!!"{w}{p}"It's goat's milk, packed with nutrition!{w}1,000 GP and it's yours~"{w}
note: Editorial: long vowel shown with ~ (Echo's style), not a hyphen. [proof] thousands comma, as in the corpus (1,000 / 15,000 GP).

en: Buy some?
"Yay, sold~"{w}
"Goa~atie, if you plea~se!"{w}
note: Accuracy: yagi-san is not gendered; 'Mister' added a gender (and the goat is sold as a milk goat).

en: Back Door Voice
note: ura-guchi kara kikoeru koe = 'voice heard from the back door'; shortened for the name box.

en: "BMOOOOOOOOH!!"{w}
note: The 'goat' bellows like a huge beast (see 2915).

en: You drank the milk.{w}
"Thank youuu!{w}Come again~~~"{w}
"Awww, you cheapskaaate~!!"{w}
A gigantic beast is tethered behind the shop!!{w}
Giant Beast
Sauna Vendor
"Anyone want a sauna~?{w}I'll give you a good price~"{w}
"Yes, thank you kindly!{w}That'll be 25,000 GP!!"{w}
note: [proof] thousands comma, as in the corpus (30,000 GP in slice 041).

en: "Hrrraaah!{w}One sauna, comin' riiight up!!"{w}
note: darasshaa: wrestling-style battle cry; rendered as a shout.

en:
A huge pile of lumber was stacked
in front of you.{w}
"You can build it with just nails and a hammer!{w}Thanks for your business!!"{w}
note: The joke: the 'sauna' is a pile of lumber to build yourself.

en: You couldn't carry it all.{w}
note: Probably the full-inventory branch; subject (the party) restored.

en: "What the heck!?"{w}
note: nan da sorya: vendor's reaction; branch not certain (refusal or unable to carry). Editorial: nan da sorya as a blunt exclamation in the vendor's rough voice; also fits either branch (accuracy note).
